settings.performance.batchSizeHelp: The number of subscribers to pull from the database in a single iteration. Each iteration pulls subscribers from the database, sends messages to them, and then moves on to the next iteration to pull the next batch. This should ideally be higher than the maximum achievable throughput (concurrency * message_rate).
settings.performance.cacheSlowQueriesHel: Only enable this on large databases that have slowed down significantly. Caches list subscriber counts, dashboard statistics etc.
settings.performance.concurrencyHelp: Maximum concurrent worker (threads) that will attempt to send messages simultaneously.
settings.performance.maxErrThresholdHelp: The number of errors (eg: SMTP timeouts while e-mailing) a running campaign should tolerate before it is paused for manual investigation or intervention. Set to 0 to never pause.
settings.performance.messageRateHelp: Maximum number of messages to be sent out per second per worker in a second. If concurrency = 10 and message_rate = 10, then up to 10x10=100 messages may be pushed out every second. This, along with concurrency, should be tweaked to keep the net messages going out per second under the target message servers rate limits if any.
settings.performance.name: Performance

maintenance.confirmSubscribersText: They're removed with their activity. This can't be undone.

developers.title: Developers
developers.keys.title: API keys
developers.keys.intro: Keys authenticate calls to the API with HTTP basic auth, using the key name as the username. Give each service its own key so you can rotate or revoke it without touching the others.
developers.keys.name: Name
developers.keys.nameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. It's the basic auth username.
developers.keys.rotateHelp: Issues a new secret. The old one keeps working for 24 hours so you can deploy without downtime.
developers.keys.revokeHelp: Stops the key at once. Requests with it get 403. This can't be undone.
developers.keys.scopesHelp: None are on by default; pick each one.
developers.keys.scope.keys_manage: Create, rotate and revoke API keys
developers.keys.onlyOnce: This is the only time the full key is shown. Store it in your secrets manager now.
developers.keys.stored: I've stored this key somewhere safe
developers.keys.sendTest: Send a test with this key
developers.keys.confirmRevoke: Revoke {name}? Requests with it get 403 at once. This can't be undone.
developers.keys.confirmRotate: Rotate {name}? The current secret keeps working for 24 hours.
developers.keys.confirmDelete: Delete {name}? It stops working and leaves the list.
developers.keys.emptyText: Create a key to send email from your code.
developers.keys.nameTaken: A key with that name already exists.
developers.keys.invalidName: Use 2 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
developers.keys.invalidScopes: Pick at least one valid scope.
developers.keys.legacyUsers: API users created under Users still work. New integrations should use keys.
developers.keys.legacyText: These API users predate keys and still work. Replace each with a scoped key, update your integration, then disable the user.
developers.keys.replaceAdmin: This API user has the admin role, so it can do anything. A key can only use the scopes picked here.
developers.keys.replaceUncovered: This API user can also do things a key can't. Anything using these permissions will stop working once you switch:
developers.keys.replaceDisableHelp: Leave this off until your integration uses the new key; disabling stops the old token straight away. You can disable it later under Users › API users.
developers.keys.migratedActive: Migrated from API user {name}. Its old token still works.
developers.keys.migratedDisabled: Migrated from API user {name}. Its old token is off.
developers.keys.noSecretYet: No key secret yet. Rotate to get one.
developers.keys.disableOldText: Anything still sending {name}'s old username and token stops working straight away. Use the {key} key instead.
developers.log.title: Message log
developers.log.cantResend: This message can't be resent: its original request wasn't kept.
developers.log.resentBy: Resent {id} from the message log by {name}
developers.log.emptyText: Transactional emails show up here once sent.
developers.log.bouncedText: The recipient's server returned the message.
developers.log.bouncedBlocklisted: The recipient's server returned the message. Subscriber blocklisted per your bounce settings.
developers.templates.title: Email templates
developers.templates.subject: Subject
developers.templates.plainTextHelp: Sent as the plain-text part. Template tags work here too. Leave empty to send HTML only.
developers.templates.headersHelp: Added to every message from this template. A header the API request sets replaces the one here.
developers.templates.invalidJson: Not valid JSON: it must be an object
developers.templates.previewHelp: The preview renders on the server with the sample data, exactly as the API will.
developers.templates.emptyText: A transactional template is the email your code sends through POST /api/tx.
developers.templates.leaveText: Your changes to “{name}” will be lost.
developers.templates.notTx: Only transactional templates can be edited here.
developers.templates.invalidSample: Sample data must be a JSON object.
developers.send.title: Send test
developers.send.intro: Send a real transactional email from the browser and see the exact API call it makes.
developers.send.notSubscriber: Not a subscriber. Default mode only sends to subscribers; switch the mode under Headers and options.
developers.send.notSubscriberOk: Not a subscriber. It's sent anyway in this mode.
developers.send.allVars: Valid JSON, all {n} template variables filled
developers.send.modes.fallback: Fallback: anyone, subscriber data if found
developers.send.modeHelp.default: Fails if the recipient isn't a subscriber.
developers.send.modeHelp.fallback: Uses the subscriber's data when the address is one.
developers.send.subject: Subject
developers.send.footnote: The response body is the API's own. The message ID comes from the Listnun-Message-Id header and the timeline from the message log.
developers.branding.title: Email branding
developers.branding.intro: Your logo appears in the header of every transactional email. It isn't used in campaigns or in the Listnun app.
developers.branding.logoDarkHelp: Used by email clients that support dark mode. Without it, the logo above sits on a white tile.
developers.branding.dropHelp: SVG, PNG or JPG up to 1 MB, at least {px} px wide, with a transparent background
developers.branding.badType: {name} wasn't uploaded: {type} isn't supported. Use SVG, PNG or JPG.
developers.branding.tooNarrow: {name} wasn't uploaded: it's narrower than {px} px.
developers.branding.unreadable: {name} wasn't uploaded: it couldn't be read as an image.
developers.branding.invalidLink: Use a full http:// or https:// address, or leave it empty.
developers.branding.invalidLogo: A logo needs an http:// or https:// URL.
developers.branding.invalidWidth: Width must be between {min} and {max} px.
developers.branding.darkClientNoLogo: Dark email client, no dark logo yet
developers.branding.usage: Templates show the logo where they include the {block} block.
developers.branding.usageAll: All {n} of your transactional templates do.
developers.webhooks.title: Webhooks
developers.webhooks.intro: We POST delivery and bounce events to your URL as they happen, signed so you can verify they came from Listnun.
developers.webhooks.retriesNote: Retries back off up to 24 h
developers.webhooks.noDeliveriesText: Send a test event, or wait for the next message.
developers.webhooks.verify: Verify the {header} header with your secret.
developers.webhooks.verifyHow: The header is t=<unix time>,v1=<signature>. Compute HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" with your signing secret, compare it to v1, and reject timestamps more than 5 minutes old.
developers.webhooks.urlHelp: Must be HTTPS and answer within 10 seconds with a 2xx.
developers.webhooks.eventHelp.message_bo: Hard or soft bounce, with the SMTP reply
developers.webhooks.rotateText: Deliveries are signed with the new secret straight away. Update your endpoint first or its checks will fail.
developers.webhooks.deleteText: It stops receiving events and its delivery history is removed.
developers.webhooks.emptyText: Get delivery and bounce events at your own URL.
developers.webhooks.backoff: Backoff: 4 min, 15 min, 1 h, 4 h, then every 6 h up to 24 h.
developers.overview.title: Overview
developers.overview.intro: Send receipts, password resets and alerts from your own code through the transactional API.
developers.overview.stepKeyText: One key per service, with the tx:send scope.
developers.overview.stepKeyHelp: Keys authenticate your code. The secret is shown once, so keep it in your secrets manager.
developers.overview.stepTemplateText: The email your code sends, with variables for its data.
developers.overview.stepTemplateHelp: Templates use .Tx.Data for the data your code sends and .Subscriber for the recipient.
developers.overview.stepTestText: Call POST /api/tx from your code or the browser.
developers.overview.stepTestHelp: Run this with your key. The message appears in the log within seconds.
developers.overview.stepLogText: See delivery status and the exact payload.
developers.overview.stepLogHelp: Every message has a timeline from accepted to delivered or bounced.
auth.forgotHelp: Enter your account's email and we'll send you a link to choose a new password.
auth.setupHelp: Set a password for your account.
auth.strength1: Too short: use at least 8 characters
auth.strength2: Fair: add length or mixed characters
campaigns.confirm.running.title: Send “{name}”?
campaigns.confirm.running.text: It goes out to {n} subscribers now. You can pause it while it sends.
campaigns.confirm.paused.title: Pause “{name}”?
campaigns.confirm.paused.text: Sending stops after the messages already in flight. You can resume it later.
campaigns.overview.pausedText: Paused {date} after {sent} of {total} emails. The other {left} people in {lists} are still waiting.
campaigns.overview.resumeText: Sending picks up where it stopped, with the {n} people still waiting.
campaigns.confirm.scheduled.title: Schedule “{name}”?
campaigns.confirm.scheduled.text: It sends automatically at its send time.
campaigns.confirm.draft.title: Unschedule “{name}”?
campaigns.confirm.draft.text: It goes back to draft and won't send until you schedule or send it again.
campaigns.confirm.cancelled.title: Cancel “{name}”?
campaigns.confirm.cancelled.text: Sending stops for good. Subscribers who haven't received it won't. This can't be undone.
campaigns.confirm.delete.title: Delete “{name}”?
campaigns.confirm.delete.text: The campaign and its stats are removed. Emails already sent aren't affected.
campaigns.confirm.deleteMany.title: Delete {n} campaigns?
campaigns.confirm.deleteMany.text: They're removed with their stats. Emails already sent aren't affected.
campaigns.confirm.noTest: You haven't sent a test of this version.

campaigns.formatInContent: Change the format in the Content step; switching converts the content.
campaigns.audienceHelp: subscribers across {n} list(s). Someone on several lists gets it once; blocklisted and unsubscribed are excluded.
campaigns.plainTextNone: Not set. Clients that can't show HTML get none.

campaigns.checkSubjectMissing: Add a subject and from address.

campaigns.tracking.pixelsHelp: For ad and analytics platforms that count opens with an image. Many email apps block images until the reader allows them, so these counts run low.

campaigns.tracking.checkReplies: Replies are recorded here, then forwarded to your Reply-To address.
